title: Well-Architected overview (framework and review workflow)
hook: The AWS Well-Architected Framework organizes cloud design into six pillars with actionable best practices. A Well-Architected Review asks structured questions so you find high-risk gaps before customers do.

blocks.text: The framework is a lens for tradeoffs across six pillars: Operational Excellence, Security, Reliability, Performance Efficiency, Cost Optimization, and Sustainability. The Well-Architected Tool stores workloads, runs questionnaires, and tracks High-Risk Issues (HRIs). Lenses such as SaaS and Serverless add domain-specific questions.

entries.plainDefinition: Design focus area with principles and questions
entries.example: Security pillar covers identity and data protection

entries.plainDefinition: Answer that violates best practice and needs remediation
Bounded system under review — accounts, regions, dependencies

blocks.text: Senior interviews expect pillar language with evidence. Production teams run quarterly Well-Architected Framework Reviews (WAFR) before major launches. Enterprise customers map your controls to Security and Reliability pillars.

blocks.title: Interview framing
blocks.body: Say: six pillars, review questions, HRIs — framework is continuous improvement, not a one-time checkbox.

sections.heading: How it works step by step

items.title: Define workload boundary
items.body: Scope environment, accounts, regions, and dependencies.

items.title: Answer pillar questions
items.body: Complete questionnaires in Well-Architected Tool or workshop.

items.title: Identify HRIs
items.body: Flag high-risk answers — missing backups, open ingress, no runbooks.

items.title: Remediate and milestone
items.body: Fix HRIs, create milestone snapshot, re-review quarterly.

blocks.title: Pitfalls to avoid
blocks.body: Treating framework as launch-only checklist. Claiming compliance without backup restore proof or alarm runbooks.

blocks.text: How to prove it in production: map HRIs to AWS Config rules, CloudWatch alarm coverage, and backup job success metrics. Mature teams block prod deploys while Security HRIs remain open.

blocks.title: What gets you rejected in interviews
blocks.body: Saying you follow all pillars perfectly — rejected. Strong answer: pillars conflict; document tradeoffs and residual risk.

interviewTakeaways: Six pillars + review questions + HRIs — continuous improvement lens.
Perfect scores on all pillars are impossible — document tradeoffs.
Link HRIs to Config rules and alarm dashboards in production.
60s: Framework evaluates design via six pillars. Tool tracks workloads and HRIs. Lenses add SaaS context. Prioritize fixes by business risk.
Follow-up: which pillar conflicts most with your architecture?
commonPitfalls: Claiming compliance without evidence — rejected; need restore tests and runbooks.
Strong answer: pillar, principle, tradeoff, proving metric.
Ignoring Sustainability when customers require carbon reporting.
